title: Simplify Spark failure diagnosis in Fabric (Preview)
summary: Microsoft introduces the Fabric Spark Operations Skill, an open-source, AI-assisted diagnostic tool that queries Fabric's Spark monitoring APIs to turn a failed notebook, pipeline, or session into a plain-English, severity-ranked root-cause report.
audience: Data engineers and on-call operators who currently triage Spark failures manually across the Spark Monitor, executor logs, and Spark Advisor, plus anyone building AI-assisted ops tooling on top of Fabric.
why_it_matters: It replaces multi-tool manual log correlation with a single natural-language diagnostic pass, and because it is open-sourced as a GitHub skill it can be run from common AI coding assistants rather than only inside the Fabric portal.
takeaways: The Fabric Spark Operations Skill is a read-only, AI-assisted diagnostic layer over Fabric's existing Spark monitoring APIs.
It resolves workspace/item identifiers from natural-language descriptions rather than requiring GUIDs or manual portal navigation.
It can trace a failure across the full chain from pipeline activity down into the underlying Spark session.
For deep analysis it can copy event logs to OneLake and spin up a local Spark History Server container.
It is explicitly a preview capability and is distributed as an open-source GitHub project, not a built-in Fabric UI feature.

claims.text: The Fabric Spark Operations Skill is a preview, read-only, AI-assisted diagnostic tool that resolves workspace and item identifiers from a plain-English description and queries Fabric's Spark monitoring APIs to produce a severity-ranked diagnostic report.

The skill supports scenarios including workspace-wide Spark health review, root-cause analysis of a failed notebook run, tracing a pipeline failure down to its underlying Spark session, run-history pattern analysis, Livy session triage, and diagnosing lakehouse table maintenance/load failures.
The skill can detect stuck, zombie, or otherwise unhealthy Livy sessions that are consuming cluster capacity without being productive.

For performance diagnosis, the skill surfaces data skew, memory pressure, and cluster sizing issues (under- or over-provisioned compute) with recommended fixes, rather than requiring manual inspection of stage metrics.

For deeper analysis the skill can copy Spark event logs to OneLake and launch a local Spark History Server container, giving full Spark UI features (DAG visualization, SQL query plans, task-level metrics) without needing Fabric portal access.

Underlying Spark session monitoring data is retained for up to 30 days; if a run has aged out of retention, the skill falls back and still surfaces what data remains available, including the failed notebook's own run snapshot.

The Fabric Spark Operations Skill is open-source, published as part of the skills-for-fabric toolkit on GitHub, and is designed to be invoked from AI coding assistants (including GitHub Copilot, VS Code, and Claude) after authenticating with az login.
